read.ko: Herc는 이 파티에서 두 개의 턴테이블을 동시에 사용하여 동일한 레코드 판 두 개를 재생한 다음, 브레이크라는 드럼 연주 구간을 연장시키기 위해 두 레코드판을 번갈아 다루었다.
read.en: At this party, using two turntables at the same time, Herc played two copies of the same record and then switched between them to extend the drum section known as the break.

read.ko: 사람들은 더 이상 레코드판이 다 돌아간 후 디제이가 LP 디스크를 교체하는 동안 춤을 멈출 필요가 없어졌다.
read.en: No longer did people have to stop dancing at the end of the record while the DJ changed the LP disc.

read.ko: Kool Herc의 디제잉 스타일은 힙합 음악과 브레이크 댄스의 부상에 빠르게 영향을 미쳤다.
read.en: Kool Herc's style of DJing quickly became influential in the rise of hip-hop music and breakdancing.

read.ko: 브레이크 구간은 노래에서 가장 기대되는 부분이 되었다.
read.en: The break section became the most anticipated part of a song.

read.ko: 사람들은 춤꾼들의 원을 만들어 브레이크 구간 동안 각자의 춤 실력을 뽐내곤 했다.
read.en: People would form dancer circles and use the break to show off their individual dancing skills.

read.ko: Kool Herc는 자신의 음악에 맞추어 춤추는 사람들을 브레이크 보이와 브레이크 걸의 줄임말로 비보이와 비걸이라고 불렀다.
read.en: Kool Herc named the people dancing to his music B-Boys and B-Girls, short for Break-Boys and Break-Girls.

read.ko: 이들은 거리에서 무리 지어 춤을 추면서 거리의 댄스 경연 문화를 구축하기 시작했다.
read.en: These people began to dance in groups in the streets and build a street dance battle culture.

read.ko: Kool Herc와 같은 디제이들은 관중의 흥을 돋우기 위해 노래의 악기 연주 구간 동안 박자와 라임을 넣은 말을 했다.
read.en: DJs like Kool Herc would speak in rhythm and rhyme over instrumental parts of songs to excite the crowd.

read.ko: 그들은 "리듬에 맞춰"와 "멈추지 마!"와 같은 문구들을 소리치곤 했다.
read.en: They would shout phrases like "To the beat" and "You don't stop!"

read.ko: 이것이 랩, 즉 엠씨잉의 시작이었다.
read.en: This was the beginning of rapping or MCing.

read.ko: 디제이들은 자신이 디제잉과 리듬감 있는 외침을 동시에 할 수가 없을 때, 친구에게 파티에서 청중에게 말하는 역할 즉 사회자 곧 엠 씨의 역할을 부탁했다.
read.en: When DJs couldn't do both DJing and rhythmic shouting at the same time, they asked a friend to take the role of addressing the audience, that is, of the Master of Ceremonies or MC, at their parties.

read.ko: 이 별도의 역할이 엠씨잉이 된 것이다.
read.en: This separate role became MCing.

read.ko: 그러면 힙합이라는 말은 어디에서 유래한 걸까?
read.en: Then where did the word hip-hop originate from?

read.ko: 정확한 유래는 아무도 모르지만, 힙합이라는 단어는 어느 블록 파티에서 처음 사용되었다고 한다.
read.en: Nobody knows the exact origin, but it is said that the word hip-hop was first used at a block party.

read.en: A young man at the party was about to join the army.

read.ko: 그의 좋은 친구이자 그 파티의 엠씨가 군 교관처럼 박자에 맞춰 무대를 가로질러 움직이면서 "힙합 힙합 힙합"을 외침으로써 그 청 년에게 자유의 시절이 끝났음을 장난스레 상기시켰다.
read.en: His good friend, the MC of the party, reminded him in a jokey way that his days of freedom were over by moving across the stage like a military instructor to the beat, chanting, "Hip- hop-hip-hop-hip-hop."

read.ko: 청중들은 그것을 좋아했다.
read.en: The crowd loved it.

read.ko: 그 후 엠씨들은 파티에서 "힙, 합, 히피 투더 히피 합밥", "내가 말했지 힙합이라고, 힙빗, 힙비딥비, 힙합합이라고, 그럼 너도 멈추지 마"와 같은 새로운 대사를 시도했다.
read.en: After that, MCs tried out new lines at parties like "Hip, hop, hippy to the hippy hop-bop," "I said a hip-hop, a hibbit, hibby-dibby, hip-hip-hop and you don't stop."

read.ko: 그러한 대사들은 랩의 표준적인 부분이 되었으며, 최초의 힙합 앨범 <Rapper's Delight(래퍼의 기쁨)>(1979)에서 가사의 일부로 들어갔고, 이 앨범은 즉각적인 성공을 거두었다.
read.en: Such lines became a standard part of rap and were included in the lyrics of the first recorded hip-hop album, Rapper's Delight (1979), which was an immediate success.

read.ko: 새로운 음악과 춤은 매우 빠르게 퍼져 나갔다.
read.en: The new music and dancing spread very fast.

read.ko: 1980년대 뉴욕에서는 설명할 수 없는 급격한 폭력 사건 감소가 있었다.
read.en: There was a sharp unexplained decline in violence during the 1980s in New York.

read.ko: 한 경찰관은 거리에 있는 한 소년에게 이유를 아냐고 물었다.
read.en: One police officer asked a boy on the street if he knew why.

read.ko: 그 소년은 "그건 그들이 춤추고 있기 때문이죠"라고 말했다.
read.en: The boy said, "It's because they're dancing."

read.ko: 초기 힙합의 파티 구호로 출발한 랩 가사는 일반적으로 다 함께 즐거운 시간을 갖자는 내용과 디제이나 래퍼의 능력을 뽐내는 내용에 초점을 두었다.
read.en: Rap lyrics, which started as the party chants of early hip- hop, typically focused on having a good time together and boasting about the ability of the DJ or the rapper.

read.ko: 그러나 1980년대 힙합 음악의 부상 시기에 중요한 변화가 일어났다.
read.en: However, a significant shift occurred during the rise of hip- hop music in the 1980s.

read.ko: 가장 중요한 것은, 1982년 그룹 Grandmaster Flash and Furious Five의 노래 <The Message(메시지)>의 등장이 획기적이 었다는 점이다.
read.en: Most importantly, the appearance of The Message by the group Grandmaster Flash and Furious Five in 1982 was groundbreaking.

read.ko: 이 노래의 강력한 가사는 게토에서 태어나 이등 시민으로 살다가 죽어야 했던 소년의 슬픈 이야기를 포함하여 게토에서의 삶의 가혹 한 현실을 자세히 묘사했다.
read.en: This song's powerful lyrics detailed the harsh realities of life in the ghetto, including the sad story of a boy who was born there and had to live and die as a second-class citizen.

read.ko: 파티를 통해 평화를 창조하는 것이 본래 목표였던 힙합은 이 노래를 통해 불의에 저항하는 새로운 사회 비판의 전통을 시작했다.
read.en: With this song, hip-hop, whose original aim was creating peace through partying, started a new tradition of social criticism against injustice.

read.ko: <The Message>는 역사상 가장 영향력 있는 랩 싱글 중 하나가 되었고, 1980년대와 1990년대에 인종 차별에 맞서는 많은 힙합 노래가 뒤를 이었다.
read.en: The Message became one of the most influential rap singles of all time, and was followed by many hip-hop songs that confronted racial discrimination in the 1980s and 1990s.

read.ko: 그와 동시에, 리듬감 있는 박자와 랩이 어우러진 그들의 음악은 사람들을 움직이게 하고 춤추게 만들었다.
read.en: At the same time, their music with its rhythmic beat and rapping made people move or dance.

read.ko: 사람들은 비트에 맞춰 몸을 움직이면서 사회적 메시지를 들었다.
read.en: People heard the social message while moving to the beat.

read.ko: 또한 힙합 가사에 점차 새로운 태도가 나타났는데 그것은 '존경'으로 요약될 수 있다.
read.en: Also, a new attitude gradually emerged in hip-hop lyrics, which can be summarized as "respect."

read.ko: 힙합 음악은 서로에 대한 존경, 특히 힙합의 선구자들에 대한 존경을 표현하는 한 방법이 되기 시작했다.
read.en: Hip-hop music began to be a way to express respect for one another, and particularly for hip-hop pioneers.

read.ko: 래퍼들에게 그 선구자들은 고난과 불의를 딛고 계속 나아가 새로운 음악과 문화를 창조해낸 영웅들이다.
read.en: For rappers, the pioneers are heroes who overcame hardship and injustice and went on to create new music and culture.

read.ko: 그러므로 많은 힙합인들은 자신들이 이 영웅들에게 아무리 큰 존경심을 가져도 지나치지 않다는 데 동의한다.
read.en: Therefore, many hip-hoppers agree that they cannot have too much respect for these heroes.

read.ko: 힙합 장르의 역사를 요약할 때 자주 사용되는 '무에서 유를'이라는 어구 또한, 매우 제한된 자원에도 불구하고 게토에서 새로운 문화를 일구어낸 초기 힙합인들에 대한 존경의 표현이기도 하다.
read.en: The phrase "something from nothing," often used to summarize the genre's history, is also an expression of admiration for early hip-hoppers, who developed a new culture in the ghetto despite very limited resources.

read.ko: 래퍼들은 또한 그들 자신도, 어쩌면 청중들도, 그 선구자들과 비슷하게 고통을 겪고 살아남았다는 느낌을 자랑스럽게 표현했다.
read.en: Rappers also proudly expressed their feeling that they, too, and perhaps the audience, had suffered and survived in a similar way to the pioneers.

read.ko: 그렇기 때문에 존경의 메시지는 자기 자신의 가치 그리고 타인에 대한 존경 둘 다에 관한 것이다.
read.en: This is why the message of respect is about both self-worth and respect for others.

read.ko: 힙합에서 존경이라는 개념의 중요성은 아무리 강하게 강조해도 지나치지 않다.
read.en: The importance of the idea of respect in hip-hop cannot be emphasized strongly enough.

read.ko: 2001년 5월 16일 유엔에 제출된 '힙합 평화 선언문'은 힙합을 국제적인 평화 문화로 공식 인정했다.
read.en: "The HipHop Declaration of Peace," presented to the UN on May 16th, 2001, officially recognized hip-hop as an international culture of peace.

read.ko: 이 문서는 브롱스에 평화를 가져오려 한 힙합 원래의 사명을 우리에게 상기시키고 힙합 역사에 대한 전세계적인 존중을 암시한다.
read.en: This document reminds us of hip-hop's original mission to bring peace to the Bronx, implying global respect for hip-hop history.

read.ko: 힙합 아티스트 Kendrick Lamar가 2018년 퓰리처 음악상을 수상했을 때, 그것은 또 하나의 중요한 사건이었다.
read.en: When hip-hop artist Kendrick Lamar was awarded a Pulitzer Prize for Music in 2018, it was another important event.

read.ko: 그것은 언더그라운드 음악으로 시작된 힙합이 클래식 음악 같은 주요 예술 형식으로 자리 잡았다는 것을 의미했다.
read.en: It meant that hip-hop, which started as underground music, had become a major art form like classical music.

read.ko: 힙합 음악이 1970년대에 평화를 위한 문화 운동의 일환으로 탄생했다면, 오늘날 점점 더 많은 사람들이 힙합을 자신을 표현하고 불 의에 맞서 싸우고 사회적 메시지를 통해 변화를 가져오고, 그러면서도 여전히 음악에 몰두하면서 타인과 연결되는 하나의 강력한 수 단으로 여긴다.
read.en: If hip-hop music was born as part of a cultural movement for peace in the 1970s, today more and more people regard it as a powerful means to express oneself, fight against injustice, bring about change through social messages, and still be engaged with music and connected to others.

read.ko: 그 독특함과 커지는 매력으로 인해 힙합은 계속해서 세계적인 현상이 되고 있다.
read.en: With its unique and growing appeal, hip-hop continues to be a global phenomenon.

read.ko: 라임은 일반적으로 단어의 마지막 소리를 반복하는 것이다.
read.en: A rhyme is usually the repetition of the final sound of a word.

read.ko: 가장 흔하게는, 그것은 시나 노래에서 행들의 마지막 위치에 음악적 효과를 주기 위해 의식적으로 사용된다.
read.en: Most often, it is consciously used for a musical effect in the final position of lines within poems or songs.

read.ko: 랩 가사에서 라임이 사용되는 세 가지 방식을 살펴보기로 하자.
read.en: Let's look at three ways that rhyme is used in rap lyrics.

read.ko: 첫째, 두 행이 서로 라임을 이루는 단어들로 끝이 나면 '엔드 라임'이라고 하는데, 이것이 라임의 가장 대표적인 종류이다.
read.en: First, if two lines finish with words that rhyme, this is called an end rhyme, which is the most representative kind of rhyme.

read.ko: 다음의 예를 소리 내어 읽어 보라.
read.en: Try reading the following example aloud.

read.ko: 우리 집은 아주 커 넌 꼭대기를 볼 수가 없어
read.en: My house is so big you cannot see the top

read.ko: 지붕에서 뛰어내리지 마 그럼 꽤 오래 떨어져
read.en: Don't jump off the roof that is quite a long drop

read.ko: 라임을 이루는 두 단어 'top'과 'drop'은 끝소리 'op'를 공유한다.
read.en: The two rhyming words "top" and "drop" share an ending sound "op."

read.ko: 둘째, 단어들은 같은 행 내에서 라임을 이룰 수 있다.
read.en: Second, words can rhyme within the same line.

read.ko: 이 경우에는 '내부 라임'이 만들어지는데, 한 행의 중간에 위치한 단어와 그 행 혹은 그 다음 행에 있는 다른 단어를 포함한다.
read.en: This creates an internal rhyme, which involves a word in the middle of a line and another word in the same or the next line.

read.ko: 예를 들면
read.en: For example,

read.ko: 그들은 결코 배우지 못할 거야 자기 차례 기다리는 법을
read.en: They're never gonna learn how to wait their turn

read.ko: 셋째, 래퍼들은 불완전한 라임을 자주 사용한다.
read.en: Third, rappers often use imperfect rhymes.

read.ko: 예를 들어, ' start', ' sport', 'straight'는 정확히 라임을 이루진 않지만 비슷한 /s/ 소리 및 /t/ 소리의 패턴을 만든다.
read.en: For example, "start," "sport," and "straight" do not exactly rhyme, but they create a pattern of similar sounds /s/ and /t/.

read.ko: 대부분의 불완전한 라임은 자음은 동일하지만 모음 소리가 다르거나, 혹은 그 반대이다.
read.en: In most imperfect rhymes, the consonants are identical while the vowel sounds are different, or the other way round.

read.ko: 라임을 이루는 일련의 단어들을 큰소리로 말하면 리듬감 있는 패턴 또는 '흐름'이 만들어진다.
read.en: When a sequence of rhymed words is spoken aloud, it creates a rhythmic pattern or "flow."

read.ko: 이는 노래가 안정된 박자를 유지하도록 돕고, 귀를 즐겁게 하며, 감정을 불러 일으킨다.
read.en: This helps the song keep a steady beat, pleases the ear, and evokes emotions.

read.ko: 그러므로 당신이 랩을 만들 때 라임을 넣는 것은 당신의 목소리를 더 힘있게 만들면서 듣는 이들에게 다가가도록 하는 멋진 방법인 것이다.
read.en: So, if you create a rap, rhyming is a great way to make your voice stronger and reach your listeners.

para.en: Imagine an urban area that is fast becoming a slum after an economic recession. Businesses close their doors and building owners have left. The area is full of abandoned buildings. There is no heating even in winter. Only those who can't afford to move out remain. Unemployment is high, many gangs emerge, and gang violence between young people becomes an everyday thing. Despair is on every street corner. One day, however, a gang called the Ghetto Brothers, which is respected because of its free meal and medical care programs, decides to stop fighting and instead persuade young people to unite and create a better community. They suggest a peace treaty. "This is for peace, men. The violence took away our brothers. We're not gangsters anymore. We've got to make this town a better place to live." Thanks to these new voices, gang leaders from all over the area sign the treaty. Never again will they use violence to solve their disputes. This is the Bronx in the New York of the early 1970s, where hip-hop music was born as a major part of a new culture of peace created by African Americans and immigrants. The story of hip-hop, now one of the world's most dominant music genres, is a fascinating one. Let's explore it.

After the peace treaty, the gangs that had fought one another started partying together. Abandoned buildings and parking lots were used for events called block parties. What eventually emerged from these parties? A vibrant youth movement called hip-hop culture, based on DJing, breakdancing, MCing, and graffiti. It replaced gang violence with music, dance, art, and style. The most popular block parties were those hosted by DJ Kool Herc, who is regarded as the founding father of hip-hop. Herc's party for his sister's birthday in August 1973 is now known as the birthplace of hip-hop music because of his new DJ technique. At this party, using two turntables at the same time, Herc played two copies of the same record and then switched between them to extend the drum section known as the break. No longer did people have to stop dancing at the end of the record while the DJ changed the LP disc. Kool Herc's style of DJing quickly became influential in the rise of hip-hop music and breakdancing. 129 2

The break section became the most anticipated part of a song. People would form dancer circles and use the break to show off their individual dancing skills. Kool Herc named the people dancing to his music B-Boys and B-Girls, short for Break-Boys and Break-Girls. These people began to dance in groups in the streets and build a street dance battle culture. DJs like Kool Herc would speak in rhythm and rhyme over instrumental parts of songs to excite the crowd. They would shout phrases like "To the beat" and "You don't stop!" This was the beginning of rapping or MCing. When DJs couldn't do both DJing and rhythmic shouting at the same time, they asked a friend to take the role of addressing the audience, that is, of the Master of Ceremonies or MC, at their parties. This separate role became MCing.

Then where did the word hip-hop originate from? Nobody knows the exact origin, but it is said that the word hip-hop was first used at a block party. A young man at the party was about to join the army. His good friend, the MC of the party, reminded him in a jokey way that his days of freedom were over by moving across the stage like a military instructor to the beat, chanting, "Hip-hop-hip-hop-hip-hop." The crowd loved it. After that, MCs tried out new lines at parties like "Hip, hop, hippy to the hippy hop-bop," "I said a hip-hop, a hibbit, hibby-dibby, hip-hip-hop and you don't stop." Such lines became a standard part of rap and were included in the lyrics of the first recorded hip-hop album, Rapper's Delight (1979), which was an immediate success. The new music and dancing spread very fast. There was a sharp unexplained decline in violence during the 1980s in New York. One police officer asked a boy on the street if he knew why. Rap lyrics, which started as the party chants of early hip-hop, typically focused on having a good time together and boasting about the ability of the DJ or the rapper. However, a significant shift occurred during the rise of hip-hop music in the 1980s. Most importantly, the appearance of The Message by the group Grandmaster Flash and Furious Five in 1982 was groundbreaking. This song's powerful lyrics detailed the harsh realities of life in the ghetto, including the sad story of a boy who was born there and had to live and die as a second-class citizen. With this song, hip-hop, whose original aim was creating peace through partying, started a new tradition of social criticism against injustice. The Message became one of the most influential rap singles of all time, and was followed by many hip-hop songs that confronted racial discrimination in the 1980s and 1990s. At the same time, their music with its rhythmic beat and rapping made people move or dance. People heard the social message while moving to the beat.

Also, a new attitude gradually emerged in hip-hop lyrics, which can be summarized as "respect." Hip-hop music began to be a way to express respect for one another, and particularly for hip-hop pioneers. For rappers, the pioneers are heroes who overcame hardship and injustice and went on to create new music and culture. Therefore, many hip-hoppers agree that they cannot have too much respect for these heroes. The phrase "something from nothing," often used to summarize the genre's history, is also an expression of admiration for early hip-hoppers, who developed a new culture in the ghetto despite very limited resources. Rappers also proudly expressed their feeling that they, too, and perhaps the audience, had suffered and survived in a similar way to the pioneers. This is why the message of respect is about both self-worth and respect for others. The importance of the idea of respect in hip-hop cannot be emphasized strongly enough. 131 4

"The HipHop Declaration of Peace," presented to the UN on May 16th, 2001, officially recognized hip-hop as an international culture of peace. This document reminds us of hip-hop's original mission to bring peace to the Bronx, implying global respect for hip-hop history. When hip-hop artist Kendrick Lamar was awarded a Pulitzer Prize for Music in 2018, it was another important event. It meant that hip-hop, which started as underground music, had become a major art form like classical music. If hip-hop music was born as part of a cultural movement for peace in the 1970s, today more and more people regard it as a powerful means to express oneself, fight against injustice, bring about change through social messages, and still be engaged with music and connected to others. With its unique and growing appeal, hip-hop continues to be a global phenomenon.

A rhyme is usually the repetition of the final sound of a word. Most often, it is consciously used for a musical effect in the final position of lines within poems or songs. Let's look at three ways that rhyme is used in rap lyrics. First, if two lines finish with words that rhyme, this is called an end rhyme, which is the most representative kind of rhyme. Try reading the following example aloud. My house is so big you cannot see the top Don't jump off the roof that is quite a long drop The two rhyming words "top" and "drop" share an ending sound "op." Second, words can rhyme within the same line. This creates an internal rhyme, which involves a word in the middle of a line and another word in the same or the next line. For example, They're never gonna learn how to wait their turn

Third, rappers often use imperfect rhymes. For example, "start," "sport," and "straight" do not exactly rhyme, but they create a pattern of similar sounds /s/ and /t/. In most imperfect rhymes, the consonants are identical while the vowel sounds are different, or the other way round. When a sequence of rhymed words is spoken aloud, it creates a rhythmic pattern or "flow." This helps the song keep a steady beat, pleases the ear, and evokes emotions. So, if you create a rap, rhyming is a great way to make your voice stronger and reach your listeners. 132
